title: CloudNote plans and pricing
body: CloudNote has four plans. Free: 1 GB storage, 2 devices, no version history. Pro: $8 per user per month or $80 per year, 50 GB storage, unlimited devices, 30-day version history. Team: $12 per user per month or $120 per year, 200 GB pooled storage, admin console, shared notebooks. Enterprise: custom pricing with SAML SSO, audit log and a signed DPA. Annual billing is charged as ten months, so two months are free.

title: You were charged twice in the same period
body: Duplicate charges are almost always a retried authorisation from your bank rather than two subscriptions. Open Settings > Billing > Invoices and compare the invoice ids. If two invoices share the same period and amount, the second is a duplicate and is refunded automatically within 5 to 7 business days. If only one invoice exists, the second entry on your statement is a pending authorisation that will drop off. Contact support with both invoice ids if neither applies.

title: Refunds and the 14-day money-back guarantee
body: A first purchase of Pro or Team can be refunded in full within 14 days of the charge. Renewals are outside the guarantee. Request a refund from Settings > Billing > Request refund, or reply to your invoice email. Approved refunds return to the original payment method in 5 to 10 business days. Refund decisions outside the 14-day window are made case by case by the billing team and cannot be issued automatically.

title: Failed payment and the 7-day grace period
body: If a renewal payment fails, CloudNote retries on days 1, 3 and 5 and emails you each time. Your plan stays fully active for a 7-day grace period. After that the workspace downgrades to Free and anything above the Free storage limit becomes read-only for 30 days. Updating your card in Settings > Billing > Payment method during either window restores the plan immediately with no data loss.

title: Switching between monthly and annual billing
body: Switch in Settings > Billing > Change plan. Moving from monthly to annual charges the annual price immediately and credits the unused part of the current month against it. Moving from annual to monthly takes effect at the end of the paid year; no partial refund is issued for the remaining months. Seat count changes are prorated to the day on both cycles.

title: Invoices, receipts, VAT and GST
body: Every charge produces a PDF invoice in Settings > Billing > Invoices, downloadable for 7 years. Add or correct a company name, address and tax id under Billing details; changes apply to future invoices and cannot be applied retroactively. VAT or GST is added where your billing country requires it and is shown as a separate line. A valid tax id in a reverse-charge jurisdiction removes the tax line from the next invoice.

title: Cancelling a subscription
body: Cancel in Settings > Billing > Cancel plan. Cancellation stops future renewals; the plan stays active until the end of the paid period, so there is no immediate loss of access. At period end the workspace becomes Free and data above the Free limit is read-only for 30 days before deletion. Export your notes first from Settings > Export if you want a copy.

title: Seats and per-seat billing on Team
body: Team plans bill per occupied seat. Adding a member charges a prorated amount for the rest of the current period immediately. Removing a member frees the seat and credits the unused portion to your next invoice. Invited members who have not accepted do not occupy a seat. Seat totals are visible in the admin console under Members.

title: Notes are not syncing between devices
body: Sync requires a signed-in account and network access. Check the sync indicator in the sidebar: a red dot means the last sync failed. Fix in order: confirm you are signed into the same account on both devices, pull down to force a sync, confirm you are under your plan storage limit because a full workspace pauses uploads, then sign out and back in on the stale device. Free accounts sync at most 2 devices, so a third device will not receive updates.

title: Why you see a Conflicted copy note
body: When the same note is edited on two devices before either syncs, CloudNote keeps both versions rather than discarding an edit. The newer edit keeps the original title and the other is saved beside it as 'Conflicted copy'. Nothing is lost. Merge manually, then delete the conflicted copy. Conflicts are much rarer if you let a device finish syncing before editing elsewhere.

title: Desktop app crashes on launch
body: A crash at launch is usually a corrupted local cache, not lost data; your notes live on the server. Quit the app, then remove the cache folder: ~/Library/Application Support/CloudNote/Cache on macOS, %APPDATA%\CloudNote\Cache on Windows. Relaunch and let the workspace re-download. If it still crashes, install the current version from cloudnote.example/download, which resets the local database schema.

title: A note is missing: restoring from version history
body: Deleted notes go to Trash and are recoverable for 30 days from Trash > Restore. For a note that still exists but lost its content, open it and choose History to restore an earlier revision. Version history covers 30 days on Pro and Team; the Free plan has no version history, so only Trash recovery applies. If a note is in neither Trash nor history, contact support with the note title and the approximate time it disappeared.

title: Attachment uploads fail
body: Per-file limits are 25 MB on Free and 250 MB on Pro, Team and Enterprise. Uploads also fail when the workspace is at its storage limit. An upload that stalls at 99% is usually a proxy stripping the connection; retry on another network. Executable file types are rejected for safety. Check current usage in Settings > Storage.

title: Search returns nothing or misses recent notes
body: Search runs against a local index that can fall behind. Rebuild it from Settings > Advanced > Rebuild search index; expect a few minutes on a large workspace. Search covers note titles, body text and attachment filenames, but not text inside images or PDFs. Notes in Trash are excluded from results by design.

title: Offline edits are not saved
body: Offline editing is available on Pro and above. Edits made offline are queued locally and upload when connectivity returns; the sync indicator shows a pending count. Do not sign out while edits are pending, because signing out clears the local queue. On Free, offline edits are not retained and the editor is read-only without a connection.

title: Web clipper does not capture a page
body: The clipper needs the browser extension enabled for the current site and a signed-in session. Pages behind a login, infinite-scroll feeds and PDF viewer tabs frequently capture partially. Use Simplified article mode for cleaner results, or Screenshot mode when the layout matters. Sites sending a strict Content-Security-Policy can block the clipper entirely; save the page as PDF and attach it instead.

title: Resetting your password
body: Choose Forgot password on the sign-in screen and enter your account email. The reset link is valid for 60 minutes and can be used once. If it does not arrive, check spam and confirm you are using the address the account was created with. Signing in changes an existing password from Settings > Security > Change password, which signs out all other sessions.

title: Setting up two-factor authentication
body: Enable TOTP two-factor authentication in Settings > Security > Two-factor. Scan the QR code with any authenticator app and confirm one code to activate. CloudNote then shows ten single-use recovery codes: store them outside CloudNote, because they are the only way back in if you lose the authenticator. SMS second factors are not supported.

title: Lost your 2FA device
body: Use one of the ten recovery codes issued when two-factor was enabled; enter it where the app asks for a code, then immediately re-enrol a new authenticator. Each code works once. With no recovery codes left, identity verification by the support team is the only route, it is deliberately slow, and it cannot be completed over chat. Regenerate codes any time from Settings > Security.

title: Changing your account email address
body: Change it in Settings > Account > Email. A confirmation link goes to the new address and the change completes only when that link is opened, so a typo cannot lock you out. The old address receives a notification for awareness. On Team and Enterprise workspaces an administrator may have restricted email changes to the admin console.

title: Deleting your account and your data
body: Settings > Account > Delete account removes the workspace and every note. Deletion is irreversible, so export first from Settings > Export. After confirmation the workspace is disabled immediately and data is purged from primary storage within 30 days and from backups within 90. Statutory erasure requests under GDPR, UK GDPR or India's DPDP Act are handled by the privacy team, who respond within 30 days and can supply written confirmation.

title: Unfamiliar sign-in activity
body: Settings > Security > Active sessions lists every session with its device, approximate location and last-seen time. Revoke any session you do not recognise, then change your password, which signs out everything else, and enable two-factor authentication. Sign-in alert emails are on by default. Report suspected unauthorised access to security@cloudnote.example so it can be investigated rather than only closed off.

title: Transferring notebook ownership
body: A notebook owner can hand over ownership from the notebook menu under Share > Transfer ownership; the recipient must already be a member of the workspace and accept. The previous owner keeps edit access unless removed. When a member leaves a Team workspace their personal notebooks are not transferred automatically, so an administrator should reassign them from the admin console first.

title: SAML single sign-on for Enterprise
body: SAML SSO is an Enterprise feature configured in the admin console under Security > SSO. Supply your identity provider metadata URL, map the email attribute, then test with one account before enforcing. With enforcement on, password sign-in is disabled for the domain and access is governed entirely by the identity provider. Keep one break-glass administrator exempt so a provider outage cannot lock out the workspace.

title: Exporting your notes
body: Settings > Export produces a downloadable archive. Formats are Markdown with attachments in folders, PDF per note, and a browsable HTML bundle. Exports of large workspaces are prepared in the background and emailed as a link valid for 72 hours. Markdown is the right choice for moving to another tool because it preserves tags as front matter.

title: Note templates
body: Save any note as a template from the note menu under Save as template, then start new notes from Templates in the sidebar. Templates support placeholder tokens such as {{date}}, {{title}} and {{author}}, which are filled when a note is created. Team and Enterprise workspaces can publish shared templates so everyone starts from the same structure.

title: Tags versus notebooks
body: A note lives in exactly one notebook but can carry many tags, so notebooks are for structure and tags for cross-cutting themes. Nested tags use a slash, for example project/alpha, and filtering a parent tag includes its children. Rename or merge tags from the tag sidebar; renaming updates every note at once.

title: Linking notes and backlinks
body: Type [[ to link to another note by title, which creates the link in both directions. Every note has a Backlinks panel listing the notes that point at it. Renaming a note updates existing links automatically. The graph view visualises links across the workspace and is available on Pro and above.

title: AI summarize
body: AI summarize condenses a long note into key points and is available on Pro, Team and Enterprise. Select text and choose Summarize, or summarise the whole note from the note menu. Summaries are generated on demand and are not stored unless you insert them. Note content is sent to the model provider only for that request and is not used for training. Administrators can disable the feature workspace-wide in the admin console.

title: Shared notebooks and permission levels
body: Share a notebook from Share > Invite by email. Roles are Viewer for read-only, Commenter for comments without edits, and Editor for full content changes; only the owner can delete a notebook or change sharing. Team and Enterprise support link sharing restricted to the workspace domain. Permissions apply to the whole notebook, so a note needing narrower access belongs in its own notebook.

title: Version history retention by plan
body: Every save creates a revision, viewable under History on a note. Retention is 30 days on Pro and Team, custom on Enterprise, and unavailable on Free. Restoring a revision does not discard newer ones, so a restore is itself reversible. Attachments are versioned alongside note text.

title: Keyboard shortcuts and the command palette
body: Press Cmd+K on macOS or Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux to open the command palette, which reaches any note, notebook or action by typing. Common shortcuts: Cmd+N new note, Cmd+Shift+F search everywhere, Cmd+E toggle edit and preview, Cmd+Shift+L insert a note link. Remap shortcuts in Settings > Keyboard.
